# Info.plist permission strings + Privacy Manifest

Apple requires a user-facing "usage description" string for every system permission an app requests. If the string is missing, the app crashes the moment that permission is asked for. This doc lists every entry Brikk needs.

**Where these go:** `ios/App/App/Info.plist` (generated by `npx cap add ios`).

You can edit Info.plist either by:
- Right-clicking → Open As → Source Code (paste the raw XML below)
- Or using Xcode's GUI editor (the keys appear as friendly names like "Microphone Usage Description")

---

## Required permission strings

### Microphone (for voice-to-CRM)

```xml
<key>NSMicrophoneUsageDescription</key>
<string>Brikk uses the microphone for Voice-to-CRM dictation. Tap the floating microphone button to record updates about a lead. Recordings are processed for AI transcription and discarded immediately — they are never stored.</string>
```

### Speech Recognition (if you enable on-device transcription later)

```xml
<key>NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription</key>
<string>Brikk uses speech recognition to transcribe your voice notes about leads into searchable text. All processing follows our privacy policy at brikk.store/privacy.</string>
```

### Push Notifications (no Info.plist needed — uses Apple's separate APNs flow, but consent is asked via Capacitor's PushNotifications plugin)

No Info.plist string required. The system shows its own modal when the app calls `PushNotifications.requestPermissions()`.

### Camera (only if you add photo capture for lead profile pictures or property images)

```xml
<key>NSCameraUsageDescription</key>
<string>Brikk lets you attach a photo to a lead or deal so you remember who they are. Photos stay on your device and in your Brikk account — never shared elsewhere.</string>
```

### Photo Library (if you let users pick existing photos)

```xml
<key>NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription</key>
<string>Brikk lets you attach an existing photo from your library to a lead or deal. Only the photos you select are accessed.</string>
```

### Contacts (only if you ever import contacts as leads — NOT enabled today)

```xml
<key>NSContactsUsageDescription</key>
<string>Brikk can import contacts you select as leads in your pipeline. Only the contacts you tap are imported — Brikk never reads or stores your full address book.</string>
```

**Don't add this yet.** Apple has been increasingly strict about contact access. Wait until we actually ship the import feature.

### Location (NOT enabled — don't add)

Brikk doesn't use location. Do not add `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` or similar. Apple will reject the app if you declare a permission you don't actually use.

---

## ATS — Network security

Add the following to Info.plist to ensure all WebView traffic uses HTTPS:

```xml
<key>NSAppTransportSecurity</key>
<dict>
    <key>NSAllowsArbitraryLoads</key>
    <false/>
</dict>
```

This is the default but worth being explicit.

---

## Privacy Manifest (`PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`) — required by Apple as of May 2024

Apple now requires a privacy manifest in the iOS bundle that declares any "required reason APIs" your app uses. Most Capacitor apps trip at least one of these.

**Create file:** `ios/App/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`

Paste:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>NSPrivacyTracking</key>
    <false/>
    <key>NSPrivacyTrackingDomains</key>
    <array/>
    <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes</key>
    <array>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeEmailAddress</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked</key>
            <true/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes</key>
            <array>
                <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeName</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked</key>
            <true/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes</key>
            <array>
                <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePhoneNumber</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked</key>
            <true/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes</key>
            <array>
                <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeOtherUserContent</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked</key>
            <true/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes</key>
            <array>
                <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeCrashData</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeLinked</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypeTracking</key>
            <false/>
            <key>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposes</key>
            <array>
                <string>NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypePurposeAppFunctionality</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
    </array>
    <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes</key>
    <array>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons</key>
            <array>
                <string>CA92.1</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons</key>
            <array>
                <string>C617.1</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
        <dict>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType</key>
            <string>NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime</string>
            <key>NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons</key>
            <array>
                <string>35F9.1</string>
            </array>
        </dict>
    </array>
</dict>
</plist>
```

This declares:
- We collect email, name, phone, user content (lead notes/messages) — linked to user, NOT for tracking, used for app functionality
- We collect crash data — not linked, for app functionality
- We use UserDefaults, file timestamps, system boot time (standard Capacitor / WebView APIs) — with Apple's approved reason codes

## Background Modes — push notifications

If you enable push notifications, also add in Xcode:

1. Click the **App** project → **Signing & Capabilities** tab
2. Click **+ Capability** in the top left
3. Add **Push Notifications**
4. Add **Background Modes** → tick **Remote notifications**

These add to Info.plist automatically:

```xml
<key>UIBackgroundModes</key>
<array>
    <string>remote-notification</string>
</array>
```

No usage description needed for push — the system prompt handles it.

---

## URL Scheme registration (for deep links like sms: and mailto:)

The web app uses `sms:`, `mailto:`, and `tel:` links extensively (Send via Messages, Email, Call). The WebView opens these as expected, but you may need to explicitly allow them. Add to Info.plist:

```xml
<key>LSApplicationQueriesSchemes</key>
<array>
    <string>sms</string>
    <string>tel</string>
    <string>mailto</string>
</array>
```

---

## Custom URL Scheme (optional — lets the app be opened from a `brikk://` link)

Useful for OAuth callbacks, magic links, push notification deep links. Add to Info.plist:

```xml
<key>CFBundleURLTypes</key>
<array>
    <dict>
        <key>CFBundleURLName</key>
        <string>store.brikk.app</string>
        <key>CFBundleURLSchemes</key>
        <array>
            <string>brikk</string>
        </array>
    </dict>
</array>
```

This lets external apps trigger `brikk://app/leads/abc123` to open Brikk and navigate to that lead. Not required for v1.

---

## Submission checklist for permissions

Before archiving:

- [ ] All permission strings written in plain English, no jargon
- [ ] No permissions declared that the app doesn't actually use (Apple rejects this)
- [ ] PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is in the bundle and valid XML
- [ ] App Privacy questionnaire in App Store Connect matches what's in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy (Apple cross-checks)

If Apple's reviewer flags any inconsistency, this is the most common rejection reason. Read all the strings out loud — they should sound like things you'd be okay reading to a user.
